selected.name: Theory-to-Algorithm Coherence
selected.instruction: Score 10 when theoretical analysis directly determines the algorithm or predicts its behavior and the abstract connects both; score 0 when theory and proposed method are unrelated decorations.
selected.rationale: R04 derives double-descent behavior from influence-function and Hessian analysis; R22 turns a common semidefinite condition into new Lipschitz parameterizations.
member_names: Improved formal bound stated against the explicit prior bound
Strength of formal guarantees (proofs, bounds, optimality)
Theory and experiment bear on the same claim

selected.name: Precise mechanistic diagnosis before solution
selected.instruction: Score 10 if the abstract pinpoints the exact mechanism causing prior methods to fail (named, characterised, and specific) before proposing a fix. Score 0 if the problem statement is generic ('X is slow/inaccurate') with no mechanistic explanation.
selected.rationale: R02 identifies LOLA's specific 'arrogant behaviour' that is 'directly at odds with convergence,' and R45 names three precise DNC pathologies (lack of key-value separation, memory aliasing, temporal-linkage degradation) before proposing targeted fixes. The dense model rewards diagnostic precision that a scorecard might conflate with generic problem-motivation.
member_names: Diagnoses failure mechanism before presenting the fix
Names an incumbent's failure and derives the fix from it

selected.name: Prior approaches shown as special cases
selected.instruction: Score 10 if the paper's framework demonstrably subsumes multiple prior methods as special cases or instances of a single more general formulation. Score 0 if the paper proposes yet another method alongside existing ones without any unifying relationship.
selected.rationale: R53 generalises Ollivier-Ricci curvature from graphs to hypergraphs in a framework that recovers prior graph curvature as a special case, and R47 presents a generalised spherical CNN framework that 'encompasses various existing approaches.' The dense model credits unification that a scorecard counting 'novelty' generically may miss.
member_names: Prior approaches shown as special cases

selected.name: Cross-regime evidential robustness
selected.instruction: Score 10 when the method is tested across genuinely different datasets, tasks, architectures, or operating regimes with a coherent pattern of support; score 0 when evidence comes from one narrow benchmark.
selected.rationale: R13 spans long and short texts across many datasets, R20 varies architectures and tasks, and R49 studies multilingual directions and data-balance regimes.

selected.name: Explicit Resource Accounting
selected.instruction: Score 10 when computational, memory, sample, query, or parameter costs are quantified and tied to design choices; score 0 when efficiency is asserted only with vague adjectives.
selected.rationale: R15 quantifies verifier speed and network scale; R46 gives complexity reductions while explaining how larger expressive models become feasible.

selected.name: Actionable Interpretability
selected.instruction: Score 10 when interpretation reveals a concrete behavioral cause and leads to correction, diagnosis, or a design insight; score 0 when interpretation is only visualization without actionable consequences.
selected.rationale: R07 uses relevance maps to find artifacts and remove them; R42 analyzes noisy memory addressing to motivate key-value separation and de-allocation changes.

selected.name: Formal Mathematical Bridging Across Domains
selected.instruction: Score 10 if a concept from a distinct field is formally mapped to the target problem via rigorous mathematical instantiation. Score 0 if inspiration is drawn from another field superficially using loose terminology without formal mathematical mappings.
selected.rationale: The dense model credits formal mathematical mapping over superficial analogy. R09 maps adversarial defense to a game-theoretic minimax mixed strategy, and R28 maps hypergraph structure to Ollivier-Ricci curvature via optimal transport. This contrasts with the vague biological or cognitive analogies in R23 and R26.

selected.name: First-Principles Continuous Formulation
selected.instruction: Score 10 if the architecture is derived directly from first principles, such as continuous ordinary/partial differential equations or dynamical systems. Score 0 if the architecture is constructed by stacking discrete heuristic blocks based solely on empirical performance.
selected.rationale: The dense model assigns high quality to architectures rooted in continuous mathematics. R39 interprets graph convolutions as integral transforms under probability measures, and R49 designs stable graph networks through the lens of ordinary differential equations, avoiding the fragility of purely discrete architectural hacks.

selected.name: Foundational tool reusability potential
selected.instruction: Score 10 if the core technique is general enough to become a standard building block reused across many future papers and subfields (e.g., a new gradient estimator, a new optimiser, a new training trick). Score 0 if the technique is tightly coupled to one task, dataset family, or architectural variant.
selected.rationale: R49 (Gumbel-Softmax) provides a differentiable sampling mechanism reusable wherever categorical latents appear, and R50 (LAMB) provides a layerwise adaptive optimiser applicable to any large-batch training regime. The dense model perceives trans-scenario utility that a scorecard focused on within-paper results may miss.

selected.name: Axiomatic Objective Derivation
selected.instruction: Score 10 if the learning objective or loss function is rigorously derived from a stated set of mathematical axioms or desired invariance properties. Score 0 if standard off-the-shelf loss functions are used or modified via unprincipled heuristics and weighting terms.
selected.rationale: The dense model rewards losses derived from axioms rather than heuristics. R48 formulates desirable properties to measure a perturbation set and mathematically proves a CVAE satisfies them. Conversely, the dense model sees little value in R27 and R18, which rely on heuristic surrogate weighting or post-hoc regularizers.

selected.name: Component-level attribution of contribution
selected.instruction: Score 10 when the abstract separates the roles of major components and provides evidence that each addresses a stated bottleneck; score 0 when a bundled system offers no indication of which parts matter.
selected.rationale: R05 distinguishes gradient search, credit assignment, and resource constraints; R26 maps three repairs to three diagnosed memory problems; R49 analyzes the effects of routing location and language-specific capacity.

selected.name: Transferable finding about the phenomenon, not only about the artifact
selected.instruction: Score whether a reader who never adopts the method still learns something durable. 10 = the abstract reports a fact about the domain, models in general, or the problem structure that survives the paper's specific artifact, and states it precisely enough to be checked or contradicted later. 5 = an observation about the phenomenon appears but is entangled with the proposed system. 0 = every claim is of the form 'our system scores higher than theirs', with nothing asserted about the world outside the comparison.
selected.rationale: R11 reports that classifiers trained on original data fail on counterfactually-revised counterparts and vice versa, and that combined training removes sensitivity to genre mentions - facts about learned text classifiers that outlive the dataset being released (.618/.295); R50 reports that the loss function shapes double descent in finite-width networks and ties it to the Hessian spectrum at the optimum (.389/.047); R57 reports that 10-30% language-specific computation at the top and/or bottom layers is where the capacity matters and that one-to-many benefits more than many-to-one. Against them R34 and R54 assert only relative standing. A bank criterion for 'contribution' counts the artifact; the transferable fact is a different currency.
member_names: Transferable finding about the phenomenon, not only about the artifact

selected.name: Conference Boilerplate Inclusion
selected.instruction: How much of the text consists of standard conference submission boilerplate (e.g., Code of Ethics acknowledgements, 'One-sentence Summary', conflict of interest statements) accidentally included in the abstract? 0 means no boilerplate; 10 means the abstract is heavily cluttered with administrative noise. Do not judge the author's compliance, only the volume of this text.
selected.rationale: Artifacts of the submission portal or copy-paste errors by the authors leave administrative fingerprints that have zero correlation with research quality but heavily distract text models. R49 contains explicit 'Code Of Ethics' and 'One-sentence Summary' fields, clearly an artifact of the upstream submission process bleeding into the text.

selected.name: Inline mathematical notation and complexity-bound density
selected.instruction: Score how much of the abstract's visible surface is occupied by inline mathematical notation rather than prose: LaTeX-style symbols and macros, named spaces and sets, big-O or order expressions, epsilon / delta / d / k / H parameters, subscripted or superscripted variables, and bracketed theory-venue citations such as [Author, VENUE'yy]. Score 0 if there is no notation at all and the abstract is entirely prose; score 5 if notation appears occasionally, for example one complexity expression or a couple of symbols; score 10 if notation appears in most sentences and a reader must parse formulas to follow the claims. Count the notation on the page. The judge must NOT judge rigour, correctness, difficulty, or whether formalism is warranted for this topic, and must not treat notation as evidence either for or against the work being good.
selected.rationale: MODE 1 (typography and subject-matter marker). Notation-saturated abstracts sit at the very bottom of the scorecard here: R53 (dense_pct=0.278, card_pct=0.009) is dense with widetilde-O expressions, d, H and epsilon; R48 (0.474 vs 0.021) carries R^d, epsilon-coresets and bracketed SODA/FOCS citations; R04 (0.496 vs 0.120) leads with O(C^2 L^5); R43 (0.389 vs 0.047) and R36 (0.769 vs 0.316) follow the same pattern. A criterion bank written in natural language has nothing to grip when the claim is carried by a symbol, so notation density predicts a low card score for reasons that have nothing to do with the merit of the theorem.
member_names: Density of formal notation and proof-verb language
Inline mathematical notation and complexity-bound density

upstream_parent_all_members: author's subfield/training background (theory vs. applied ML) — practice in this format
writing conventions of the theory-versus-applied subcommunity that produced the work

selected.name: Release and resource signaling
selected.instruction: Score 0-10 for the extent to which the abstract advertises code, models, configuration files, datasets, videos, or other reproducibility resources; judge only the presence and prominence of these signals, never their usefulness.
selected.rationale: Resource-release language can act as an institutional or author-practice cue apart from research quality, although the underlying practice may also support genuine quality. Examples are R16's code, configuration files, and pretrained weights and R57's source code, models, ethics statement, and summary.
selected.upstream_parent: author's reproducibility practice and available resources
upstream_parent_all_members: author's reproducibility practice and available resources

selected.name: Abstract length / elaboration verbosity
selected.instruction: On a 0-10 scale, rate ONLY how long and elaborated the abstract text is (word count, number of sub-clauses/sub-claims covered), where 0 = extremely terse (roughly one to two sentences, under ~60 words) and 10 = extremely long and elaborated (many clauses and sub-claims, over ~250 words). Do NOT judge whether the length is appropriate or whether the underlying work is good; score length alone.
selected.rationale: R47 (~55 words, no elaboration) and R05 (~90 words) are both terse and both dense_high_card_low; R35 and R30 are long, heavily elaborated abstracts (multiple numbered sub-problems, many results) and both are dense_low_card_high. A scorecard built from checklist criteria plausibly needs more surface area to find things to score, independent of whether the underlying research is better; but longer abstracts could also genuinely reflect more extensive experiments, so the parent cause is ambiguous (mixed).
member_names: Sheer verbal bulk of the abstract

selected.name: Crowded-field late-synthesis vs first-mover idea framing
selected.instruction: On a 0-10 scale, rate ONLY how much the abstract frames itself as arriving late into an already-crowded space of many named/enumerated prior alternatives that it must position against, unify, or amalgamate (e.g., 'Existing methods have attempted...', 'Many...have been proposed...however none...', 'amalgamate a pool of teacher optimizers'), versus reading as a direct, minimally-contrastive presentation of one self-contained new idea. Score 0 = reads as a first, direct, minimally-contrastive presentation of an idea; 10 = reads as a late synthesis/differentiation move that explicitly catalogues and positions against many prior alternatives. Do NOT judge whether the positioning against prior work is accurate or whether the synthesis is a genuine advance; score only how much the framing reads as 'early direct idea' vs 'late crowded-field synthesis'.
selected.rationale: R39 ('Optimizer Amalgamation': explicitly amalgamating 'a pool of teacher optimizers' because 'none can offer a universal advantage') and R50 ('under a common theoretical lens' unifying convex-potential layers, AOL, and orthogonality methods) both read as late syntheses of an already-crowded space and are both dense_low_card_high, versus R47 (a short, direct, uncontested presentation of a new attention mechanism) and R33 ('we determine for the first time...'), both dense_high_card_low. This textual posture reflects where the item sits in the stream of takes on a topic, not the merit of the specific contribution, so purely a nuisance.
member_names: Crowded-field late-synthesis vs first-mover idea framing
selected.upstream_parent: position in the entry stream — how many similar prior submissions/approaches already existed when this abstract was framed
upstream_parent_all_members: position in the entry stream and submission timing
position in the entry stream — how many similar prior submissions/approaches already existed when this abstract was framed

selected.name: Enumerated contribution scaffolding and roadmap phrasing
selected.instruction: Score how much explicit enumerated scaffolding the abstract uses to present its contributions: phrases such as 'our contributions are three-fold' or 'two-fold', sequences of 'First, ... Second, ... Third, ... Fourth, ...', numbered or lettered items such as i) ii) iii) or 1) 2), and explicit roadmap sentences announcing what the paper will do in order. Score 0 when contributions are stated in flowing prose with no enumeration; score 5 when there is one ordinal sequence or a single 'we make two contributions' announcement; score 10 when the body of the abstract is organised as an explicit numbered list. Score only how much of this scaffolding is visible. The judge must NOT decide whether the enumerated contributions are substantial, whether the organisation aids the reader, or whether enumerating is good scientific practice.
selected.rationale: MODE 2 fingerprint of an unseen factor (how practised the group is at writing for this venue's review rubric). Practised submitters pre-chunk the abstract into rubric-shaped slots, which a criterion-bank scorer can tick off one at a time. R12 states 'Our contributions are three-fold' and then walks i)/ii)/iii) (dense_pct=0.291, card_pct=0.594); R28 marches through 'First / Second / Third / Fourth' (0.154 vs 0.641); R51 announces 'Our contribution is two-fold' (0.081 vs 0.564); R29 numbers its findings 1) and 2) (0.605 vs 0.906). Mixed is true and honestly so: a group that has learned the format may also genuinely do better work, so this channel belongs in the sensitivity band rather than being written off.
member_names: Enumerated contribution scaffolding and roadmap phrasing
Ordinal/enumeration scaffolding of contributions or challenges

upstream_parent_all_members: the authors' accumulated practice in this submission format; rubric-aware, reviewer-facing writing habits learned over repeated submission cycles

selected.name: Named large-scale engineering/experimental-resource markers
selected.instruction: On a 0-10 scale, rate ONLY how much the text names concrete large-scale infrastructure or resource figures (specific hardware such as 'TPU Pod', specific huge batch sizes or wall-clock training-time claims, or explicit counts of baselines/search-spaces/datasets used in a single study), where 0 = no such resource/scale figures and 10 = multiple specific large-scale resource figures are named. Do NOT judge whether the scale achieved is impressive or whether more compute makes better research; score only the presence of named resource/scale figures.
selected.rationale: R14 names specific hardware and scale ('TPUv3 Pod', batch size '32868', 'reduced from 3 days to just 76 minutes') and is dense_high_card_low; R55 advertises an unusually large experimental footprint ('12 baselines, 16 HPO search spaces and 86 datasets/tasks') and is dense_low_card_high. Both leave a textual trace of a well-resourced team, which could be a pure prestige/access signal or could genuinely enable stronger empirical work, hence mixed.
selected.upstream_parent: author's institutional resources / access to large-scale compute or experimental infrastructure
upstream_parent_all_members: author's institutional resources / access to large-scale compute or experimental infrastructure

selected.name: Diagnostic bearing of the evaluation conditions actually described
selected.instruction: Score 0-10 for how much the evaluation described in the abstract — however small or large — bears on the specific claim the abstract makes. Read the claim first, then ask: does the abstract describe at least one condition in which that claim could plausibly have failed (a harder or shifted setting, an ablation that removes the proposed ingredient, a comparison against the most obvious competing explanation or the strongest alternative a reader would think of), and does it state what was actually found there, including any limit, cost, or place where the effect was absent? 10 = a single, plainly described experiment that is clearly the one that could have broken the claim, with the outcome of that test stated in concrete terms and its boundary acknowledged — this must be reachable with no dataset names, no counts, no parameter counts, no compute figures, and no baseline tally. 5 = the described conditions are relevant to the claim and some concrete finding is reported, but nothing described could realistically have contradicted the claim, or no limit is acknowledged. 0 = nothing described could have come out otherwise, or the text reports only that the method 'improves' or 'outperforms' with no stated finding tied to the claim — score 0 even if the abstract enumerates many datasets, languages, model families, model sizes, baselines, GPU-hours, seeds, or annotators. Explicitly do NOT reward the number of settings, datasets, tasks, languages, architectures, sizes, baselines, runs, raters, or resource figures named; a long enumeration is by itself neither credit nor debit here. Do not reward technical vocabulary, formality, or length. Judge only whether what is described could have discriminated the claim, and whether the text says what it discriminated.
selected.rationale: The conjectured upstream cause (a group with the means to run wide evaluation) produces two things: real evidential leverage, and a countable pile of setting names. This component takes only the leverage, by forcing the judge to read the claim and ask whether any described condition could have falsified it and what was learned — a question a count cannot answer. Dissociation, direction one (high real, low surface): an abstract that names no benchmark and reports one experiment — 'we remove the retrieval step and the gain disappears on the held-out split we constructed to break the shortcut; the effect vanishes when inputs exceed the training length' — scores near 10 here and near 0 on the surface component, which finds almost nothing to count. Dissociation, direction two (low real, high surface): an abstract reporting 'experiments on 14 benchmarks, 6 languages, 5 model families from 1B to 70B, against 9 baselines, using 4,000 GPU-hours' with the single finding 'our method consistently improves performance' scores near 10 on the surface component and 0 here, because no described condition could have contradicted the claim and no finding beyond a direction is stated.
selected.parent: Count of enumerated evaluation settings and resource markers
member_names: Diagnostic bearing of the evaluation conditions actually described

selected.name: Enumeration count of evaluation settings and resource markers
selected.instruction: Score 0-10 by counting or estimating how many distinct evaluation settings and resource markers the text enumerates, and nothing else. Count each of: named or counted datasets or benchmarks; named tasks; named languages; named domains; named model architectures or model families; model sizes or parameter counts; transfer, zero-shot, few-shot, or cross-lingual settings named as settings; a stated number of baselines or comparison systems; and explicit scale statements such as compute used, GPU-hours, number of training runs or seeds, number of human annotators, or corpus size. 0 = no evaluation setting or resource marker of any kind is named. 2 = exactly one is named. 5 = roughly three or four distinct settings or counts appear. 8 = five to eight appear, or an explicit large count appears (for example 'twelve benchmarks'). 10 = many appear, or large counts appear across several of these categories at once. This is explicitly NOT a quality judgement. Do not decide whether the coverage is adequate, necessary, convincing, redundant, or excessive; do not consider whether anything was learned in those settings; do not consider whether the comparisons were controlled or fair; do not consider whether the claim is supported. If an item lists many settings and reports no finding at all, it must still be able to score 10. Score only the amount of enumeration present on the page.
selected.rationale: This is the pure fingerprint: the countable residue that a well-resourced or convention-fluent writing process leaves, with every trace of merit stripped out by forbidding any judgement of adequacy or of what was learned. Dissociation, direction one (high surface, low real): the '14 benchmarks, 6 languages, 5 model families, 9 baselines, 4,000 GPU-hours, consistently improves' abstract scores 10 here and 0 on D01, since nothing described could have failed. Dissociation, direction two (low surface, high real): the one-ablation abstract that names no dataset and gives no counts scores about 1 here while scoring near 10 on D01. Because the count is mechanical and the judge is barred from asking whether it earned anything, the two scores move independently and the pair can be used to separate the carrier from the substance.
selected.parent: Count of enumerated evaluation settings and resource markers
member_names: Enumeration count of evaluation settings and resource markers
selected.upstream_parent: surface carrier of bank criterion: Count of enumerated evaluation settings and resource markers

selected.name: Precision of the claim, its assumptions, and its failure regime
selected.instruction: Score 0-10 for how exactly the text pins down what is being asserted and the conditions under which it is asserted to hold. Credit, in plain prose exactly as much as in symbols: (a) a claim stated sharply enough that a reader could say what observation would contradict it; (b) the conditions, assumptions, or scope restrictions the claim depends on, stated rather than implied; (c) quantities named with their direction and, where relevant, the price paid — what gets worse, or what resource is spent, when the claimed gain is obtained; (d) an acknowledged regime in which the claim is not asserted to hold. 10 = short, symbol-free, unfashionable prose in which the assertion, the conditions it needs, the trade-off, and the regime where it fails are each unambiguous to a first-time reader. 5 = the assertion is clear but one of its conditions, costs, or failure regimes is left implicit. 0 = the reader cannot say what the text rules out — assertions such as 'we develop a principled framework that better captures the underlying structure' with no stated condition, no stated cost, no stated boundary — and this score of 0 stands even if the text is dense with theorems, lemmas, bounds, convergence rates, norms, expectations, big-O expressions, Greek letters, and displayed formulas. Explicitly do NOT reward mathematical notation, symbols, or formal-mathematical vocabulary, and do NOT penalise their absence; do not judge whether any mathematics present is correct, deep, novel, or fashionable; do not reward hedging language that merely sounds careful without naming a condition. Judge only how precisely the text fixes the assertion and the conditions attached to it.
selected.rationale: The conjectured upstream cause (a formally trained approach to the problem) yields both a genuine good — a claim whose scope and failure conditions are actually pinned down — and a typographic fingerprint of symbols and theorem-words. This component isolates the good by asking a question that plain prose can answer perfectly and that dense notation cannot answer at all: what would contradict this, and under what conditions is it asserted? Dissociation, direction one (high real, low surface): 'Our rule beats the baseline whenever the label noise is below about 20 percent and the classes are roughly balanced; above that it is worse, and it costs one extra pass over the data' contains no symbol, scores near 10 here and near 0 on D04. Dissociation, direction two (low real, high surface): an abstract packed with 'we prove a tight O(1/sqrt(T)) bound under standard regularity assumptions on the loss, establishing convergence of the proposed estimator' that never says which assumptions, never says what fails without them, and never names a cost, scores near 10 on D04 and near 0 here.
selected.parent: Extent of formal notation and mathematical vocabulary
member_names: Precision of the claim, its assumptions, and its failure regime

selected.name: Density of formal vocabulary and mathematical notation on the page
selected.instruction: Score 0-10 for the raw extent of formal-mathematical vocabulary and notation in the text, counting or estimating only. Count occurrences of formal-mathematical vocabulary such as theorem, lemma, proposition, corollary, proof, bound, convergence, rate, assumption, regularity, convexity, smoothness, optimality, minimax, complexity, estimator, guarantee, and close relatives; and any inline notation such as Greek letters, single-letter variable names, subscripts or superscripts, norms, expectations, probability symbols, big-O or Omega expressions, inequalities, set or operator symbols, or displayed formulas. 0 = none of these markers appears anywhere. 3 = one or two isolated markers in the whole text. 7 = markers recur across several sentences. 10 = such vocabulary and notation are dense from the first sentence to the last. This is explicitly NOT a quality judgement. Do not consider whether the formalism is correct, rigorous, necessary, well used, or informative; do not consider whether anything is actually proved; do not consider whether symbols are defined or whether assumptions are stated; do not consider whether the prose is clear. An item saturated with symbols that states nothing a reader could check must still be able to score 10.
selected.rationale: This is the carrier alone: a typographic and lexical count, with every route to merit closed off by explicitly forbidding any assessment of correctness, necessity, definedness, or informativeness. Dissociation, direction one (high surface, low real): the 'tight O(1/sqrt(T)) bound under standard regularity assumptions' abstract that never names an assumption or a failure regime scores 10 here and 0 on D03. Dissociation, direction two (low surface, high real): the symbol-free noise-threshold sentence scores 0-1 here and near 10 on D03. Since one score is produced by counting glyphs and the other by asking what the text rules out, an item can sit at either corner, which is what makes the pair usable as separated components.
selected.parent: Extent of formal notation and mathematical vocabulary
member_names: Density of formal vocabulary and mathematical notation on the page
selected.upstream_parent: surface carrier of bank criterion: Extent of formal notation and mathematical vocabulary

selected.name: Substantiated range: variation reported across conditions that could differ
selected.instruction: Score 0-10 for how well the text establishes the range over which its result actually holds. Credit three things: (a) the described conditions differ along a dimension that could plausibly change the outcome, and the text says what that dimension is (for example language typology, input length, domain shift, model scale, annotation density) rather than merely listing near-duplicate conditions; (b) the text reports how the result varied across those conditions — where it held, where it shrank, where it reversed — rather than reporting a single pooled direction; (c) the text names a boundary: a condition under which the result is not claimed. 10 = exactly two conditions, chosen because they differ in the way that matters, with the text stating that the effect held strongly in one, weakened in the other, and naming where the claimed range stops — reachable with no lists, no counts, and no coverage vocabulary. 5 = a real dimension of variation is identified and some differential result is reported, but no boundary is named. 0 = no dimension of variation is identified and only a pooled direction is reported, for example 'consistently outperforms strong baselines across a wide range of tasks, languages, and model scales' — this 0 stands however many datasets, languages, domains, architectures, or baselines are listed. Explicitly do NOT reward the number of datasets, tasks, domains, architectures, baselines, or settings named, and do NOT reward conventional coverage vocabulary such as extensive, comprehensive, large-scale, multilingual, cross-domain, zero-shot, or at scale; do not penalise their absence. Do not reward the mere assertion that results are consistent; consistency asserted without any reported variation across a named dimension is not evidence of range.
selected.rationale: The conjectured upstream cause here is convention — writers who have absorbed audience expectations both produce genuinely better-mapped generality and produce the enumerative style those expectations reward. This component keeps only the mapped generality: it asks whether the conditions differ along a dimension that could have changed the answer, whether the answer is reported to have changed, and where the claim stops — none of which a list length can supply, and all of which two well-chosen conditions can. It is distinct from D01, which asks whether any single condition could have falsified the claim; this one asks how far the claim has been traced and where it breaks. Dissociation, direction one (high real, low surface): 'We test on one high-resource and one morphologically rich low-resource language; the gain holds for the former, halves for the latter, and disappears once the training set falls below a few thousand sentences' names two conditions and no coverage vocabulary — near 10 here, near 1 on D06. Dissociation, direction two (low real, high surface): 'Extensive experiments on 12 benchmarks spanning 6 languages, 4 domains, and 5 architectures show our approach consistently outperforms strong baselines' scores 10 on D06 and 0 here, because no dimension of variation, no heterogeneity, and no boundary is reported.
member_names: Substantiated range: variation reported across conditions that could differ

selected.name: Extent of coverage listing and breadth vocabulary
selected.instruction: Score 0-10 by counting or estimating how much the text lists coverage and how much breadth-signalling vocabulary it uses. Count two things together: (i) the number of listed datasets, benchmarks, tasks, domains, languages, model architectures, model sizes, baselines, or experimental settings, whether named individually or given as a count ('twelve benchmarks', 'six languages'); and (ii) occurrences of breadth-signalling phrasing such as extensive experiments, comprehensive evaluation, a wide range of, across diverse, large-scale, multilingual, cross-domain, cross-lingual, zero-shot, in-the-wild, at scale, or thorough ablations. 0 = the text lists no coverage items and uses no such phrasing. 3 = one or two items or one such phrase. 6 = several listed items, or a coverage phrase plus a short list. 10 = long enumeration across multiple categories, or several breadth phrases stacked together, or both. This is explicitly NOT a quality judgement. Do not decide whether the listed coverage is adequate, appropriate, persuasive, redundant, or padded; do not consider whether the conditions differ in any meaningful way; do not consider whether any result across them is reported; do not consider whether the breadth vocabulary is warranted. An item that lists a dozen benchmarks and reports only 'consistently outperforms' must still be able to score 10.
selected.rationale: This is the conventional fingerprint by itself — list length plus the stock phrases the convention supplies — with every judgement of warrant explicitly forbidden, so no merit can leak in. Dissociation, direction one (high surface, low real): the 'extensive experiments on 12 benchmarks spanning 6 languages, 4 domains, 5 architectures, consistently outperforms' abstract scores 10 here and 0 on D05, since it names no dimension of variation, reports no heterogeneity, and states no boundary. Dissociation, direction two (low surface, high real): the two-language abstract that reports the gain halving on the morphologically rich language and vanishing below a data threshold uses no breadth vocabulary and lists two items, scoring about 1-2 here while scoring near 10 on D05. Counting phrases and counting listed items is mechanical and independent of whether any variation was reported, so both corners are attainable.
member_names: Extent of coverage listing and breadth vocabulary
selected.upstream_parent: surface carrier of bank criterion: Evaluation-breadth signaling
